_doc: New Zealand, written by hand for the ranking and the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-14). Multi-day treks (Great Walks) are trail pages of app/trails. Sources per area; scores on docs/RANKING.md.

areas.season: December to March is summer, the busiest; November and April are quieter and still mild.
areas.sleep: The waterfront and Viaduct, or Ponsonby for cafés.

items.name: Ferry to Devonport, up Mount Victoria, then the Sky Tower
items.why: Ten minutes by ferry to a Victorian seaside village, a volcano cone with the city across the water, then the city from 328 m up.

steps.what: Walk up Mount Victoria, a volcanic cone

items.name: A day on Waiheke Island: vineyards and beaches
items.why: Forty minutes by ferry to an island of vineyards, olive groves and white beaches like Oneroa and Palm Beach.

areas.season: December to March is summer, the busiest; November and April are quieter and still mild.
areas.sleep: Paihia, by the wharf; Russell across the water is quieter.

items.name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
items.why: Where Māori chiefs and the British Crown signed the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840, the founding document of New Zealand: the carved meeting house, the great war canoe, the museum.

steps.what: The cultural performance in the meeting house
The war canoe on the shore

items.name: Hole in the Rock and dolphins by boat
items.why: Out among the bay's 144 islands to the pierced rock at Cape Brett, with dolphins on the way and a stop on Urupukapuka island.

items.name: Opua forest lookout walk
items.why: Up through the bush behind Paihia to a view over the bay and Russell.

areas.season: December to March is summer, the busiest; November and April are quieter and still mild.
areas.sleep: Hahei, between the two: very busy from Christmas to the end of January.

items.name: Cathedral Cove by boat or kayak
items.book: The walking track from Grange Road was closed by landslips in 2023: check DOC whether it has reopened, otherwise go by boat or kayak.
items.why: A limestone arch between two white beaches in a marine reserve, reached by sea from Hahei.

items.name: Dig your own pool on Hot Water Beach
items.best: Two hours each side of low tide
items.book: Bring or hire a spade; the water at the source is 64°C, dig a little away from it.
items.why: Two hot springs come up through the sand two hours each side of low tide: dig a hole and lie in it, the surf a few metres away.

areas.season: All year: the caves are the same in the rain.
areas.sleep: Waitomo village, or as a stop between Auckland and Rotorua.

items.name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves by boat
items.why: A walk through the limestone, then a silent boat in the dark under a ceiling of thousands of glowworms.

items.name: Black water rafting in Ruakuri Cave
items.why: Float on an inner tube down an underground river, jump off subterranean waterfalls, glowworms above.

items.name: Ruakuri Cave walk
items.why: A spiral entrance into a cave the Māori found 400-500 years ago, with streams and glowworms on walkways.

areas.season: All year; the thermal areas steam best on cold mornings.
areas.sleep: By the lake or near the centre: you smell the sulphur everywhere.

items.name: Te Puia: Pohutu geyser and Māori arts
items.why: The Whakarewarewa valley of boiling mud and the Pohutu geyser, with the national school of Māori carving and weaving; a hāngī dinner and a performance in the evening.

items.name: Wai-O-Tapu and Waimangu volcanic valley
items.book: Wikivoyage last listed Wai-O-Tapu as closed for renovation: check it is open.
items.why: Pools of every colour, the orange-rimmed Champagne Pool, and Waimangu, a valley born from the 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera.

items.name: Hobbiton movie set
items.why: The Shire of the Lord of the Rings films on a sheep farm near Matamata: hobbit holes, the mill, a drink at the Green Dragon.

items.name: Polynesian Spa by the lake
items.why: Hot mineral pools on the shore of Lake Rotorua, open until late.

areas.season: All year; summer for the lake.
areas.sleep: Taupō town, on the lakefront.

items.name: Huka Falls and Craters of the Moon
items.why: New Zealand's biggest river forced through a narrow rock cleft in a roar of blue water, then a boardwalk among steaming craters.

steps.what: Aratiatia rapids: the dam gates open at 12:00

items.name: Orakei Korako, the hidden valley
items.why: A boat across the lake to geysers, silica terraces and a cave with a hot pool inside.

areas.season: The Crossing is a summer walk, November to April; in winter it needs ice axe and crampons. Weather turns fast: one day spare.
areas.sleep: National Park village or Whakapapa, with a shuttle to the start.

items.name: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing
items.book: Book the shuttle: it drops you at Mangatepopo and collects you at Ketetahi. Do not leave a car at Mangatepopo.
items.why: 19.4 km across an active volcanic landscape: the Red Crater, the Emerald Lakes, the cone of Ngauruhoe; one of the great day walks on Earth.

steps.what: Up the valley to the Devil's Staircase
South Crater, then the ridge to Red Crater
Down the scree to the Emerald Lakes
Blue Lake, then the long descent

items.name: Taranaki Falls from Whakapapa
items.why: Through beech forest and over old lava flows to a 20 m waterfall, Ruapehu behind.

areas.season: All year; windy in every season.
areas.sleep: Te Aro or the waterfront, everything on foot.

items.name: Te Papa, the national museum
items.why: New Zealand's museum by the harbour: Māori treasures and a marae, the colossal squid, the earthquake house.

items.name: Cable car, Botanic Garden and Mount Victoria lookout
items.why: Up the red cable car to Kelburn, down through the gardens, then the city and harbour from Mount Victoria.

items.name: Zealandia ecosanctuary
items.why: A fenced valley in the city where New Zealand's rare birds live as before the rats; the night tour finds kiwi.

areas.season: December to March is summer, the busiest; November and April are quieter and still mild.
areas.sleep: Picton, at the ferry.

items.name: The Cook Strait ferry through Queen Charlotte Sound
items.why: The crossing from Wellington ends in an hour of green fjords to Picton.

items.name: Kayak in the Marlborough Sounds
items.why: Paddle the sheltered bays from Picton or Anakiwa, dolphins and birds around.

areas.season: October to April; the coast is mild all year.
areas.sleep: Kaiteriteri or Marahau, at the park's door.

items.name: Water taxi up the coast, walk back
items.why: Golden beaches and granite coves: a water taxi drops you up the coast track and you walk back through the bush from bay to bay.

steps.what: Water taxi from Marahau or Kaiteriteri
Dropped at Anchorage or Bark Bay
Lunch and a swim on a beach
Back to Marahau, or picked up at a bay

items.name: Sea kayak in Abel Tasman
items.why: Paddle along the coast to seal colonies and beaches only reachable by sea.

areas.season: All year: the whales are here every month. Tours stop in rough seas: one day spare.
areas.sleep: Kaikōura town, along the Esplanade.

items.name: Whale watching from Kaikōura
items.best: The morning, when the sea is calmer
items.book: Book ahead; trips are cancelled in rough seas.
items.why: Sperm whales feed all year over a deep canyon just off the coast, with snowy mountains behind.

items.name: Point Kean seals and the Peninsula Walkway
items.why: Fur seals asleep on the rocks at the car park, then along the clifftops to South Bay.

items.name: Swim with dusky dolphins
items.why: In a wetsuit among hundreds of dusky dolphins, or just watch them from the boat.

areas.season: All year; the west coast is wet in every season.
areas.sleep: Punakaiki, between the forest and the sea.

items.name: Pancake Rocks and the blowholes
items.best: High tide with a westerly swell
items.why: Limestone stacked like pancakes, the sea blasting up to 15 m through the blowholes at high tide.

items.name: Pororari River track
items.why: Up a gorge of limestone walls and nikau palms, the river green below.

areas.season: All year; it rains a lot, but clear days are sharp. One day spare for the helicopters.
areas.sleep: Franz Josef or Fox village, both at the glacier's foot.

items.name: Franz Josef glacier valley walk
items.why: Along a rocky riverbed between waterfalls to a viewpoint on the glacier coming down from the Alps.

items.name: Lake Matheson at dawn
items.why: A 4.4 km loop around a dark lake with Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman mirrored in it.

items.name: Heli-hike or snow landing on the glacier
items.book: Flights go only in clear weather: book for the first morning, keep a spare day.
items.why: A helicopter up to the ice, then a guided walk among blue caves and crevasses, or a landing on the névé.

items.name: Glacier hot pools
items.why: Hot pools in the rainforest of Franz Josef village.

areas.season: December to March for walks, July to September for skiing.
areas.sleep: Wanaka town, on the lake.

items.name: That Wanaka Tree and the lakefront
items.why: A lone willow standing in the lake, the most photographed tree in the country, at sunrise.

items.name: Rob Roy Glacier walk
items.why: Up a valley of beech forest in Mount Aspiring National Park to a hanging glacier: Wanaka's favourite day walk.

items.name: Puzzling World
items.why: The leaning tower, the great maze and the illusion rooms.

areas.season: December to March for the lakes and walks, July to September for skiing.
areas.sleep: In town or along Frankton road, with the lake view.

items.name: Skyline Gondola to Bob's Peak
items.why: The lake, the town and the Remarkables from above; ride the luge down.

items.name: TSS Earnslaw across Lake Wakatipu
items.why: A coal-fired steamship of 1912 to Walter Peak high-country farm.

items.name: Arrowtown and the Gibbston wine valley
items.why: A gold-rush village of 1862 with its Chinese settlement, then pinot noir in the Kawarau gorge, past the first bungy bridge.

items.name: Shotover Jet
items.why: A jetboat at full speed through the narrow canyon of the Shotover river, spinning 360°.

items.name: Kawarau Bridge bungy
items.why: 43 m from the bridge where commercial bungy began in 1988.

areas.season: All year. Milford is wet most days: the waterfalls are best in rain. Snow can close the road in winter: one day spare.
areas.sleep: Te Anau: two hours from Milford, against more than twelve hours there and back from Queenstown.

items.name: The Milford Road and a cruise on Milford Sound
items.book: Book the cruise; fill the tank in Te Anau, fuel in Milford is limited.
items.why: Two hours of the road through Fiordland, Mirror Lakes and the Homer tunnel, then a cruise under Mitre Peak, rising 1,692 m from the water, to the Tasman Sea.

steps.what: Leave Te Anau on the Milford Road
Back on the road, stops at the Chasm

items.name: Te Anau glowworm caves
items.why: Across the lake by boat, then on foot and by small boat inside a living cave of glowworms.

items.name: Doubtful Sound
items.why: Across Lake Manapouri and over a pass to a fjord three times longer than Milford and far quieter.

items.name: Te Anau bird sanctuary
items.why: Takahē, a blue flightless bird thought extinct until 1948, on the lakeshore walk.

areas.season: October to April for the walks; snow can close the road. Clouds hide the peak often: one day spare.
areas.sleep: Mount Cook village, or Twizel 50 minutes away.

items.name: Hooker Valley track
items.why: 10 km return over three swing bridges to Hooker Lake, icebergs floating under Aoraki / Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak.

steps.what: Second swing bridge, the Mueller glacier lake

items.name: Tasman Glacier viewpoint
items.why: A short climb to the lake of New Zealand's longest glacier, grey ice and floating bergs.

items.name: Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre
items.why: The story of the climbers of Aoraki, with a planetarium, in the Hermitage hotel.

areas.season: All year; lupins in November-December; the clearest skies in winter.
areas.sleep: Tekapo village, facing the lake.

items.name: The Church of the Good Shepherd and Mount John
items.why: A stone chapel framing a turquoise lake, then the walk up Mount John for the whole Mackenzie basin.

items.name: Stargazing on Mount John
items.book: Book the Dark Sky Project tour; it runs only on clear nights.
items.why: A tour at the observatory in a dark-sky reserve: the Milky Way, the Magellanic clouds.

items.name: Tekapo Springs
items.why: Hot pools at 35-37°C looking up the lake.

areas.season: All year.
areas.sleep: The centre, rebuilt after 2011, walkable.

items.name: Christchurch after the earthquake
items.why: The Cardboard Cathedral by Shigeru Ban, the earthquake memorial on the Avon, the Gothic Arts Centre and the botanic gardens.

items.name: International Antarctic Centre
items.why: A polar storm room, a Hägglund ride and little blue penguins, by the airport the Antarctic flights leave from.

areas.season: November to March; wild and windy all year.
areas.sleep: Owaka or Curio Bay.

items.name: Nugget Point, waterfalls and Curio Bay
items.why: A lighthouse over rock islets full of seals, two forest waterfalls, and a petrified forest on the beach at Curio Bay where yellow-eyed penguins come ashore at dusk.

steps.what: Curio Bay: the petrified forest at low tide
Penguins coming ashore, from a distance
